h.Independente da embalagem (\"comportamen: Whatever the packaging ("human behavior", "progressive", "algorithm-aligned"), the core of the service is always the same: reviews from people who were never customers of your business.
h.Não importa se a conta é \"real\" e \"at: It doesn't matter if the account is "real" and "active". What makes a review legitimate isn't the profile of the person writing it — it's the genuine experience behind it. A review from someone who never set foot in your shop, never used your service and was paid to write five stars is, by definition, fake. And that's exactly what Google prohibits.
h.1. Você perde tudo de uma vez. O Google: 1. You lose everything at once. Google doesn't notify you when it removes reviews. You only find out when you look at your rating and it has plunged. Businesses that bought reviews wake up with their score wiped out, sometimes worse off than when they started.
h.2. Seu perfil pode ser sinalizado ou sus: 2. Your profile can be flagged or suspended. In the most serious cases, Google doesn't just delete the fake reviews — it marks the profile as suspicious. Regaining the algorithm's trust after that is slow and sometimes irreversible.
h.3. Você se expõe juridicamente. Manipula: 3. You expose yourself legally. Manipulating your reputation to influence consumers' buying decisions may amount to misleading advertising (under Brazil's Consumer Defense Code) and unfair competition. It's a risk most business owners don't even consider, but it's there.
h.Aqui está a parte que poucos contam: o G: Here's the part few people tell you: Google encourages reviews. It just wants them to be real.
